title: Release Process
concept: The complete XIOM project release process — versioning, changelogs, tagging, building, and publishing to the package registry.
why: Shipping software is different from building it. A structured release process ensures your users get reliable, documented, reproducible releases every time.
theory:
## From Code to Release

### Semantic Versioning (SemVer)

```
v1.2.3
│ │ │
│ │ └─ PATCH: bug fixes, no API change
│ └─── MINOR: new features, backward compatible
└───── MAJOR: breaking changes
```

### Release Checklist

1. **Update version** in `package.xi`
2. **Update CHANGELOG.md** with all changes
3. **Run full test suite** — all platforms
4. **Verify contracts** — `xiom verify src/`
5. **Build release** — `xiom build --release`
6. **Tag the commit** — `git tag v1.2.3`
7. **Push and create release** on GitHub
8. **Publish package** — `xiom pkg publish`

### package.xi

```xiom
package myapp
  version "1.2.3"
  author "Team XIOM"
  description "A sample XIOM application"
  license "MIT"
  repository "https://github.com/user/myapp"
  entry "myapp.main"

  deps [
    { name: "xiom.json", version: "^0.2.0" },
    { name: "xiom.http", version: "^0.3.0" },
  ]
```

### CHANGELOG.md

```markdown
## [1.2.3] - 2026-07-15

### Added
- New `User::from_json` constructor
- Support for WebSocket reconnection

### Fixed
- Memory leak in HTTP connection pool (#142)
- Stack overflow in recursive JSON parser (#138)

### Changed
- Default timeout increased from 30s to 60s
```

### Automated Release Script

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -e
VERSION=$1

xiom fmt --check src/
xiom lint --deny-warnings src/
xiom test
xiom verify src/ || echo "Warning: some contracts unverified"
xiom build --release

git tag "v$VERSION"
git push origin "v$VERSION"

xiom pkg publish
```

### Release vs Debug

| Aspect | Debug | Release |
|--------|-------|---------|
| Optimization | -O0 | -O3 |
| Contracts | Checked | Stripped (unless --runtime-contracts) |
| Debug info | Full | Stripped |
| Binary size | Large | Small |
| Use case | Development | Production |

tips: Follow SemVer strictly — your users depend on version numbers to know what changed
Always update CHANGELOG.md BEFORE tagging — it's part of the release commit
Build releases in CI — never build from a developer's machine (reproducible builds)
Test releases on all target platforms before publishing — one broken platform blocks adoption
common_mistakes: Skipping the CHANGELOG — users need to know what changed
Bumping major version for minor changes — breaks downstream clients unnecessarily
Publishing without running the test suite — broken releases damage trust
